problem: Existing VLN agents build scene memory directly from raw visual observations, so task-irrelevant cues introduce continual localization errors, and they lack transferable general knowledge priors, giving weak spatial perception in unseen environments.
motivation: Long-range instruction following requires reliable scene memory and spatial reasoning. Irrelevant objects pollute memory and hurt decisions in complex scenes, so selecting task-relevant features should improve cross-modal grounding and generalization.
key_idea: Use open-vocabulary perception to build task-oriented semantic priors that filter irrelevant objects locally, and a spatial-instruction guided dual attention to form selective goal-oriented global memory.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so ablations are not visible. The claim is that task-oriented feature selection combined with multi-level semantic modeling (local filtering plus global selective memory) improves cross-modal understanding and navigation on unseen environments.
method: Hierarchical Semantic Prior Extractor: uses open-vocabulary perception to build task-oriented semantic priors that capture critical objects.
Room-Information-Guided Filtering: uses room information to suppress task-irrelevant object features at the local level.
Spatial-Instructional Guided Dual Attention (global): uses spatial information and instruction guidance to build selective, goal- and task-oriented memory.
